attribution.reason: At update 33's saved state the braking-box row's 0.01 s endpoint tip speed is 0.5827480226234343 m/s, still far above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit, so within this horizon even instantaneous maximal-braking input does not bring endpoint tip speed near the settling limit; the probe therefore cannot carry the closed-loop settling failure on this mechanism and no local-probe result can certify it.

The recorded-input row shows a higher 0.01 s endpoint tip speed (0.6851514257340946 m/s) and a smaller speed change (-0.7719393694366347 m/s) than the braking-box row (0.5827480226234343 m/s; -0.874342772547295 m/s) at the same state, so the applied command is locally not equivalent to maximal instantaneous braking; a single-state 10 ms projected probe cannot show that this local shortfall drives the closed-loop settling failure, and the box itself still fails the limit.

Terminal and late tip speeds far exceed the 0.02 m/s settling limit while terminal position is within tolerance, and the saved recipe weights velocity/tip-speed terms small (velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0) against terminal_weight 5.0; raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance or actual contributions, and no iteration traces exist to measure them, so this stays unresolved.

Effective horizon falls from 8 to 3 control intervals across the sampled late updates, and the bounded check shows a single 0.01 s step cannot reduce endpoint tip speed toward 0.02 m/s even under braking-box input, so reduced lookahead could limit braking/tip-speed shaping; the retained signals do not separate horizon from solver stops, weighting or model mismatch.

Matched projected-GVS versus recorded-backend world-tip differences are small but nonzero (~0.006 m at update 27) and one-step velocity differences reach 0.14969247760063253 m/s at update 29, and at update 33 the projected-state tip speed 1.4570907951707293 m/s is below the recorded backend 1.5810152739742807 m/s; a bounded 0.01 s probe cannot show this mismatch dominates settling.

35 deadline misses and mean update wall time 17.075238151415917 s against a 0.01 s control period are recorded, but scheduling is synchronous: controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps, so wall-clock deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time and cannot directly cause the physical settling failure.

Projected-GVS versus recorded-backend comparisons at updates 27 to 29 show small but nonzero world-tip differences (0.0059230819406683064 m at update 27) and one-step velocity-vector difference norms 0.021386880777076088 m/s (update 28) and 0.14969247760063253 m/s (update 29); at update 33 the saved projected state's tip speed of 1.4570907951707293 m/s differs from the recorded backend tip speed of 1.5810152739742807 m/s at t=0.33 s.

At update 30 the recorded applied tension on tendon channel 0 is 7.990411884680996 N against the 8.0 N per-tendon limit listed for all six tendons in inventory source.force_limits.

At update 33's saved projected state (t=0.33 s) the bounded check's recorded-input row holds the update-33 applied tension [5.661220351760543, 3.988726293001102, 5.0287952725384195e-05, 1.4347363175658354, 1.0812420082241823, 0.003992529299500661] N over a 0.01 s horizon with 0.002 s implicit-Euler steps and predicts a 0.01 s endpoint tip speed of 0.6851514257340946 m/s, endpoint tip position [0.2811575960633344, 0.035432429209937166, 0.19430133932320742] m, endpoint tip error 0.009842592258858245 m and a 0.01 s speed change of -0.7719393694366347 m/s, with input bounds satisfied.

The same check's instantaneous braking-box row, run at the same saved state and the same 0.01 s horizon with 0.002 s implicit-Euler steps, predicts a 0.01 s endpoint tip speed of 0.5827480226234343 m/s, an endpoint position drift of 0.005559344630308817 m and a 0.01 s speed change of -0.874342772547295 m/s with input bounds satisfied (row computation 1.5369500000961125 s); the payload is flagged advisory_only and describes instantaneous affine-input deceleration at a fixed recorded pose/rate, not an experimental braking claim.

At the same saved state and 0.01 s horizon the recorded-input row's 0.01 s endpoint tip speed (0.6851514257340946 m/s) and speed change (-0.7719393694366347 m/s) differ from the braking-box row's (0.5827480226234343 m/s; -0.874342772547295 m/s): the recorded endpoint speed is higher and its speed change is smaller in magnitude, while both endpoint speeds remain far above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.

limitations: The bounded check is one saved projected state (update 33), one 0.01 s horizon, model.gvs@1.0.0 and 0.002 s implicit-Euler steps; instantaneous affine-input deceleration need not persist during a held-input rollout and the payload is advisory only, with no experimental braking claim.

Both check rows leave 0.01 s endpoint tip speed far above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit, so the probe cannot reproduce or explain the closed-loop settling failure; a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot explain an entire settling failure, and a single-state probe cannot certify a dominant cause.

The probe state is the saved projected GVS state, not the complete backend state; its tip speed 1.4570907951707293 m/s differs from the recorded backend tip speed 1.5810152739742807 m/s at t=0.33 s, and the payload's state_scope is 'recorded projected GVS state, not complete backend state'.
Historical optimizer iterations and full warm plans are not retained (source.historical_full_plans retained=false), so cost-term contributions and seed selection remain unmeasured.

The braking-box row's endpoint tip position and tip error leaves are not exposed as context fact handles here, so no recorded-minus-braking endpoint tip position difference is asserted; no derived value was produced.
Deadline misses are synchronous wall-clock scheduling observations and, per the host, must not be read as physical feedback delay; mean update wall time is not a control-loop delay.
Single execution and model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause, and no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution capability exists in the inventory.
Only update 33's saved projected state was consumed by the check; the other 34 records of source.saved_projected_states were not read.
recommended_actions: Keep every settling explanation open; the spent bounded check is a single-state, single-horizon, projected-model result and cannot certify a dominant cause.

Do not adopt control-parameter changes on this evidence: raw objective weights (velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0) do not establish cost-term importance, and the check shows even an instantaneous braking-box input leaves 0.01 s endpoint tip speed far above 0.02 m/s.
